title: The environment kinds are fenced BEFORE they exist: MCP-excluded and human-only
description:
Prerequisite LEAF carved out of task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41 by worker-caece97b (acting as architect on a claimed PLANNING row), 2026-09-05, because a2409cba measured 13 forced file edits against the 10-file hard cap and its obvious seam turned out to be WELDED SHUT. Parent chain: SPIDR child 1b of task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612.

WHY THE OBVIOUS SPLIT IS IMPOSSIBLE, so nobody re-proposes it. `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238` asserts SET-EQUALITY between the v2 command plane's registry keys and `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` (minus the one named `planning.submit_decomposition` exception):

    expect([...v2.registry.keys()].sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)
      .filter((kind) => kind !== "planning.submit_decomposition").sort());

So a row that adds the two kinds to `PAYLOAD_KEYS` WITHOUT registering both handlers reds immediately. The vocabulary half and the registry half must land in ONE row. That is a measured fact, not a preference - re-check line 238 before disputing it.

WHAT CAN LAND ALONE IS THE FENCE, AND ONLY IN THIS DIRECTION. Excluding a kind that does not exist yet is a safe no-op, while registering a kind before excluding it is a SECURITY HOLE for the duration of a row. Measured at `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:84-90`: `WIRED_KINDS` is `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` FILTERED by `!MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.includes(kind)`. A name in the exclusion roster that is absent from `PAYLOAD_KEYS` filters nothing and changes no served surface. `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` (`orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195`) is a deny-set for the same reason. THEREFORE THIS ROW GOES FIRST and task-a2409cba depends on it - never the reverse.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: adding `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` to `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` and to `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, plus the two test rosters that will otherwise red on the counts. NO vocabulary, NO PAYLOAD_KEYS, NO registry, NO handler, NO generated client - all of those are task-a2409cba.

MEASURED SEAMS (by worker-caece97b at HEAD f3b94eaa, commands and results):
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:60-83` - `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` is a frozen array of exactly SIX kinds: approval.decide, approval.decide_intent, product_contract.answer_clarification, cutover.activate, graph.approve, repository.publish. Each carries a comment giving its standing contract; follow that convention.
- `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts:322-324` - TWO HARD COUNTS, `expect(expectedExclusions).toHaveLength(6)` and `expect(MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS).toHaveLength(6)`, plus a sorted set-equality against a locally transcribed list. Both become 8 and the list gains both kinds. This file is invisible to a grep for the new kind literals and is the single most likely thing to be missed.
- `orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195-208` - `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, the ONE definition (`agent-wrapper.ts:24` re-exports it; do not look for a second).
- `grep -rln HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` -> exactly three files: agent-spawn-contract.ts, agent-wrapper.ts (re-export only), and `http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` (the only asserter). Check that last one for a count or an exact-roster arm before assuming it stays green.

THE HEADER OF mcp-tool-allowlist.ts CARRIES A STANDING CONTRACT about RE-ADMITTING kinds (removing them from the roster). This row only ADDS, which that contract permits and in fact anticipates. Do not read it as a bar on additions.
definitionOfDone: `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` are both members of `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS`, each with a one-line comment naming WHY in the file's existing convention: an agent that could set an environment variable could set one the deploy then delivers to a production process.
Both kinds are members of `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` in `orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` - the ONE definition.

`daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` is updated at BOTH hard counts (6 -> 8) and in its transcribed exclusion list, and the sorted set-equality arm passes. Prove the arm still bites: delete ONE of the two new kinds from the production roster and confirm the test REDS, then restore.

PROVE THE ADDITION IS A NO-OP ON THE SERVED SURFACE, since the kinds do not exist yet: assert that `wiredMcpToolKinds()` is byte-identical before and after - excluding an absent kind filters nothing. Record the served-kind COUNT from before and after; they must be equal.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (path-attributed per global rail 3) and `pnpm typecheck`. `pnpm test` is NOT required: this row touches no `packages/**` and the root vitest include has no `apps/**` - say so explicitly rather than quoting a vacuous run.
taskRails: ADD ONLY. Do not remove or reorder any existing entry in either roster - `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts`'s header records a standing contract that re-admitting a kind invalidates, and a reorder is the silent edit its set-equality arms exist to catch.

NO VOCABULARY, NO PAYLOAD_KEYS, NO REGISTRY, NO HANDLER, NO GENERATED CLIENT. Those are task-a2409cba and are welded together by the set-equality arm at daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238. Touching PAYLOAD_KEYS here would red that arm.

THIS ROW MUST LAND BEFORE task-a2409cba, never after. Excluding a kind that does not exist is a no-op; registering a kind before excluding it advertises an operator-only command to every agent over MCP.
HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS has exactly ONE definition (agent-spawn-contract.ts:195); agent-wrapper.ts:24 re-exports it. Do not look for a second.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND CAPTURE THE BEFORE-STATE, NO EDITS. This row's central proof is a BEFORE/AFTER comparison, so the before-value must be captured before anything changes. (a) Write a throwaway probe that imports `wiredMcpToolKinds` from apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.js, prints `JSON.stringify(wiredMcpToolKinds())` and its `.length`, and run it. RECORD THE FULL OUTPUT AND THE COUNT IN THE STEP NOTE - quoted output alone is a lead, so also paste the probe's SOURCE inline per global rail 12, since the probe will not survive the commit. (b) `grep -n 'toHaveLength(6)' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` and `sed -n '316,325p'` on it, to confirm the two counts and the transcribed list are where this plan says. (c) `sed -n '195,209p' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` for HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. (d) Confirm the kinds are NOT yet in PAYLOAD_KEYS: `grep -n 'environment.set_variable' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` must return nothing - if it returns a hit, task-a2409cba has landed out of order and you should stop and say so.

THE MCP EXCLUSION. Add `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` to `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` in apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, in sorted position (between `cutover.activate` and `graph.approve`). Follow the file's established convention: every entry after the first carries a comment giving its standing contract, so write one that says what the fence is FOR - an agent that could set an environment variable could set one the deploy then delivers to a production process, and the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential (mcp-main.ts:112-127), so an MCP caller would arrive AS the operator and receive a real witness. Exclusion is the fence; a capability gate is not one. ADD ONLY - do not remove or reorder an existing entry, and do not act on the header's re-admission contract, which governs REMOVALS.
implementationPlan.note:
THE MCP EXCLUSION LANDED. Both kinds added to `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS`; roster is now 8.

ONE PLAN CORRECTION, made deliberately rather than silently. The step said to insert "in sorted position (between `cutover.activate` and `graph.approve`)". THAT PREMISE WAS WRONG and I checked before following it: the PRODUCTION roster is NOT alphabetical. Read at :60-81 the order is approval.decide, approval.decide_intent, product_contract.answer_clarification, cutover.activate, graph.approve, repository.publish — grouped by CONTRACT NARRATIVE, each entry sitting under the comment that explains it, not by name. Only the TEST's transcribed `expectedExclusions` list is alphabetical, and the set-equality arm sorts both sides, so source order is free. I inherited the "sorted" claim from reading the test list and wrote it into my own plan; inserting alphabetically would have split `repository.publish` from its comment and broken the file's actual convention.

So: APPENDED as a new group after `repository.publish`, with its own comment block. The test list at step 4 stays alphabetical, which is that file's convention.

THE COMMENT SAYS WHY THESE ARE A DIFFERENT CASE, because they are. Every kind already on this roster is fenced by the human-review-witness contract the header describes: the registry mints a witness on operator PRINCIPAL identity alone, so those kinds must be MCP-unreachable or the witness stops meaning anything. NOTHING IN THE ENVIRONMENT SLICE MINTS A WITNESS, so that argument does not reach it and I did not borrow it. The ground here is the payload: an agent that could set an environment variable could set one the deploy then delivers to a production process. The mechanism is shared, though, and the comment says so — `mcp-main.ts:112-127` authenticates the MCP port with the operator bootstrap credential, so an MCP caller holding it arrives AS the operator and a capability gate would wave it through. Exclusion is the fence; a capability is not one.

ADD ONLY, as the task rail requires: `git diff` on this file shows a pure insertion — 9 added lines, ZERO deleted. No existing entry removed, renamed or reordered, so the header's standing contract about RE-ADMITTING a kind (which governs removals and would require the server-set transport-origin field to land first) is untouched.

Also unchanged by construction: `WIRED_KINDS` at :84-90 filters `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` by this roster, and neither new name is in PAYLOAD_KEYS yet (step 1 (d): zero grep hits), so this addition filters nothing. Step 5 proves that against the step-1 before-value rather than asserting it.

NO EDIT to that file, which is what the plan predicted: its two arms filter offered kinds to `approval.*` (:357-361, requiring membership) and pin `planning.submit_decomposition` / `product_contract.propose_revision` as absent (:412-416). An `environment.*` name satisfies the first vacuously — it is not an `approval.` kind so the filter never yields it — and is not either compiler kind, so neither arm can see this change.

WHAT THE COMMENT RECORDS, since the two fences look redundant and a later reader will be tempted to drop one. They are not the same fence and both are wanted:
- The MCP exclusion (step 2) stops an agent REACHING the kind over a transport.
- `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` stops the WRAPPER minting an agent session to take it as staffed work.
Different actors, different failure. The first fails if a transport is added; the second fails if the offer surface ever starts offering these kinds. I said so in the comment so neither gets deleted as duplication of the other.

I also noted honestly in the comment that these two kinds differ from every existing member: the kinds already in this set have an agent-facing step the offer surface CAN present, so the deny-set is doing live work for them. These two have no agent-facing step at all today, which makes the entry belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing right now. That is deliberate — the row exists to fence the kinds BEFORE they exist — but writing "belt-and-braces" down is more useful to the next reader than implying it is currently blocking something.

comments.author: worker-caece97b
comments.content:
THE ROW'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS REFUTED BY TWO COMMITTED INVARIANTS. I filed this row, planned it, and my own premise was wrong. Measured, not argued.

THE PREMISE I WROTE: "excluding a kind that does not exist yet is a safe no-op", because `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:92-98` computes `WIRED_KINDS` as `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` filtered by the exclusion roster, so a name absent from PAYLOAD_KEYS filters nothing.

THAT HALF IS TRUE AND I PROVED IT. After adding both kinds, `wiredMcpToolKinds()` was byte-identical to the step-1 before-value, COUNT=46 both sides. The served surface genuinely does not move.

BUT THE ROSTER IS NOT A DENY-LIST OF NAMES. It means "kinds that ARE wired but are NOT advertised", and two arms in `apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` enforce exactly that, each with a comment saying why it exists:

  :101-113  "excludes kinds that are REAL vocabulary keys, and excludes them from the roster"
      for (const kind of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS) {
        expect({ kind, real: vocabulary.includes(kind) }).toEqual({ kind, real: true });
      }
    Its comment: "A MISSPELLED member would exclude nothing and leave every other arm green, so the
    roster is pinned against the vocabulary it claims to subtract from."

  :244-257  "C2 keeps every excluded kind SERVED by the registry - this closes ONE transport"
      const served: readonly string[] = [...provider.provide().registry.keys()];
      for (const kind of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS) {
        expect({ kind, served: served.includes(kind) }).toEqual({ kind, served: true });
      }
    Its comment: "the kinds leave the MCP ADVERTISEMENT and stay fully wired in the daemon... Without
    this arm, deleting them from PAYLOAD_KEYS outright would also pass C1."

A kind that does not exist in PAYLOAD_KEYS and is not in the registry fails BOTH. The very arm designed to catch a misspelling catches an unwired kind, because to that arm they are the same thing. Adding the fence early is indistinguishable from typing a name that will never exist - and that is the correct behaviour, not a defect to work around.

MEASURED, the full red set from `vitest run src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts src/mcp-main.test.ts src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts`: `Test Files 3 failed | 1 passed (4)` / `Tests 7 failed | 47 passed (54)`.
  mcp-main.test.ts            STDIO-1 omits every excluded kind ... expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-http-host.test.ts       HTTP-1 refuses tools/call ...        expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-http-host.test.ts       HTTP-2 does not advertise ...        expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  pins an EXACT frozen denominator     expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  advertises far fewer kinds ...       expected 46 to be 44
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  excludes kinds that are REAL ...     INVARIANT 1
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  C2 keeps every excluded kind SERVED  INVARIANT 2

A SECOND PLANNING ERROR OF MINE, visible in that list. I wrote in planningNotes that "mcp-main.test.ts:216 and mcp-http-host.test.ts:658 all map over MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS itself" and therefore stay green. They DO map over it - and they ALSO carry their own hard `6`. I greped for the symbol, saw a `.map(...)`, and stopped. I never opened `src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` at all, which is the file that actually owns the roster's semantics. Global rail 19 says to grep the SHAPE, not the symbol; I did the thing it warns against.

SO THE TRUE COST OF PUBLISHING THESE TWO KINDS IS ~17 FILES, not the 13 I measured: the four hard-count test files above are forced too, and they are welded to the registry wiring by invariant 2 exactly as `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238` welds PAYLOAD_KEYS to the registry.

WHAT IS STILL SAFELY DELIVERABLE, and is in the tree now: the `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` half. That roster IS a pure deny-set with no membership invariant - its only asserter (`http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts`) filters to `approval.*` kinds and to two named compiler kinds, so an `environment.*` entry is invisible to it. Verified green WITH the edit: `Test Files 5 passed (5)` / `Tests 79 passed (79)` across all five files above. The two impossible edits are reverted; `git status` shows only `M apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`.

comments.author: worker-caece97b
comments.content:
MEASUREMENT THAT INVALIDATES THIS ROW'S CENTRAL PREMISE (worker-caece97b, 2026-09-05, at HEAD 8a534255).

The plan asserts the other readers of `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` "all derive rather than transcribe, so all stay green". I ran them. **Seven arms red across THREE files the plan never names.** Verbatim:

```
FAIL src/mcp-main.test.ts > STDIO-1 omits every excluded kind ...
  AssertionError: expected 8 to be 6
FAIL src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts > excludes kinds that are REAL vocabulary keys ...
  AssertionError: expected { …(2) } to deeply equal { …(2) }
FAIL src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts > advertises far fewer kinds than the MCP package generates
  AssertionError: expected 46 to be 44
FAIL src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts > pins an EXACT, frozen exclusion denominator ...
  AssertionError: expected 8 to be 6
FAIL src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts > C2 keeps every excluded kind SERVED by the registry ...
  AssertionError: expected { …(2) } to deeply equal { …(2) }
FAIL src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts > HTTP-1 refuses tools/call for every excluded kind ...
  AssertionError: expected 8 to be 6
FAIL src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts > HTTP-2 does not advertise any excluded kind ...
  AssertionError: expected 8 to be 6
```

THIS IS NOT A COUNT BUMP. Five of the seven are SEMANTIC. The roster's contract — stated in its own header, "The command kinds this daemon WIRES but REFUSES TO ADVERTISE", and "SUBTRACTED HERE, NOT DELETED UPSTREAM. The kinds stay fully wired in `PAYLOAD_KEYS` and in the command registry" — is enforced by guards that require a member to be wired, registered, and tool-generating:
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:105-112` — every excluded kind must be a real `PAYLOAD_KEYS` key. Its comment names its purpose: a MISSPELLED member would exclude nothing.
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:242-256` (C2) — every excluded kind must be SERVED by the registry. Explicitly guards against "deleting them from PAYLOAD_KEYS outright would also pass C1".
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:126-130` and `:147-151` — the identity `wired.length === vocabulary.length - excluded.length + queries.length`, which is only true when excluded is a SUBSET of the vocabulary.
- `mcp-main.test.ts:239-241` / `mcp-http-host.test.ts` — the sweep asserts a tool was GENERATED for each excluded kind (`{generated: true, kind}`), then omitted from `allowed`.

A kind fenced BEFORE it exists satisfies none of these. Landing this half requires redefining what the roster MEANS and relaxing five guards whose job is to prove the fence is real — then a2409cba re-tightening them. That is precisely the shape this row's own planningNotes rejected: "a test whose job is to be removed is worse than none."

THE INERTNESS CLAIM (DoD 4) IS TRUE, and the red proves it. `advertises far fewer kinds` reports **actual `wiredMcpToolKinds().length` = 46**, identical to the pre-change value; only the test's REIMPLEMENTED arithmetic moved (46 - 8 + 6 = 44). The served surface does not change. So the row is safe — it is the guards, not the behaviour, that reject the intermediate state.

DoD 3's DRILL PASSED before I reverted. With both kinds added, deleting `environment.unset_variable` from the production roster red `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts:324` with `AssertionError: expected [ 'approval.decide', …(6) ] to have a length of 8 but got 7` (the value has 7 members, so it is the `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` assertion at :324, not the `expectedExclusions` literal at :323 that vitest's code frame prints first). Restored and proven twice: SHA256 `a69394f3…31386b` equal to the out-of-tree backup, and `git diff --stat` showing `8 insertions(+)`, zero deletions.

WHY THE SPLIT BUYS NOTHING. The fence-first ordering exists to avoid an advertisement window between two ROWS. There is no window if a2409cba adds the kind to `PAYLOAD_KEYS` and to `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` in the SAME commit — the kind is never advertised at any landed HEAD, and every guard above stays green because 48 - 8 + 6 = 46 still holds. Same-commit is strictly SAFER than this row's two-row ordering and costs zero guard relaxation.

mcp-tool-allowlist.ts's header carries a standing contract that RE-ADMITTING a kind (removing it from the roster) invalidates a witness contract and requires a transport-origin field to land first. This row only ADDS. Do not read that header as a bar on additions, and do not remove or reorder an existing entry.

The set-equality arm sorts both sides so it will not catch a misplacement, but the diff will read badly and the next hand-editor will trust the order.
